int_name: E LEHIGH AVE & N FRONT ST

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and signalization. However, the environment is car-centric with wide asphalt expanses, a lack of physical traffic calming, and no vertical buffers like street trees to protect pedestrians from the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Geometry
hazards.description: The wide turning radii and lack of curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure time and allow for higher vehicle turning speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or vertical element (like trees or bollards) between the sidewalk and the moving traffic, reducing the sense of safety.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalks on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a vertical buffer for pedestrians and create a visual narrowing effect for drivers to encourage slower speeds.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change that gives pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and signalized traffic control in a mixed-use urban environment. However, the very wide roadway creates a long, unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians across at least four travel lanes without a median refuge.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic in a single stage, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes and a lack of physical traffic calming measures encourage higher vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The street environment consists of a wide two-lane roadway with basic sidewalks and faded crosswalk markings. The lack of physical traffic calming and the presence of parked vehicles near the intersection create potential visibility and speed-related hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: The wide, straight lanes without traffic calming measures may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection can block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint crosswalks with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines by preventing parking too close to the corner.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically directed at the sidewalk and crossing areas to improve nighttime safety.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection featuring a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a dedicated bike lane. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the significant crossing distance and lack of pedestrian refuge islands or curb extensions increase exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a mid-point refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible, which can lead to uncertainty regarding safe crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signals that display the remaining time to cross, improving predictability for all road users.
